anomalies.observed: The 74LVC1G34 buffer U8 has its input (pin 2, type "input") on the auto-named net Net-(U8-Pad2), which is connected only to U4 pin 2 (ADM3260 primary-side SCL_2). U8's push-pull output (pin 4, type "output") is placed on net I2C_SCL, which is also driven by the ESP32 master pin M1.J1_4 (IO5/I2C_SCL) and by U3 pin 2 (SCL_2), and pulled up by R4. So the EC isolator's primary SCL is treated as the source that drives the shared bus clock.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the main (non-isolated) I2C bus connects to the primary side of U3 and U4, with the ESP32 (M1.J1_4) as the only master driving SCL. If a clock buffer is used at all, its input must come from the master (ESP32 SCL) and its output must drive the bus/slaves; it must never be driven by an isolator's slave-side SCL pin. The buffer input must also have a defined level (pull-up) if the source is open-drain.

evidence.quote: Primary (non-isolated) side of U3 and U4 (ADM3260 isolators), which bridge through to the isolated pH/EC domains.

anomalies.impact: I2C_SCL is driven simultaneously by the ESP32's open-drain SCL pin and by U8's push-pull output (and U8's input has no pull-up), so the clock line will contend/shoot-through and the EC isolator U4 never receives the master clock (its SCL pin is only the buffer input). EC (EZO-EC) communication fails and the shared clock bus is disturbed, while U3/pH may still work because U3's SCL is wired directly.

anomalies.observed: T3 (AON6407, a P-channel MOSFET) is wired as a high-side element in the main 24 V feed: source (pin 2) on /+24V_F, drain (pin 3) on the +24V bulk rail, gate (pin 1) on /G_RPP (Zener D3 to GND and R7 to /+24V_F). It is not connected to the ATO_VALVE net. The ATO solenoid valve is instead switched by T5 (AO3400A N-FET, gate on /G_ATO driven through R10 from ATO_VALVE and pre-driven by T4).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the ATO solenoid-valve switch is T3: "T3 — AON6407 ... ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch ... drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904)", and lists the ATO valve as powered "via T3/T4 switch, ATO_VALVE net". T3 should therefore be the transistor that the ATO_VALVE net controls, not a pass element in the 24 V feed.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: The intended ATO-valve driver (T3) is instead placed in series with the entire 24 V rail (always on, gate clamped by D3/R7), and the valve is driven by a different device (T5). If T3's placement/type differs from the intended part, the ATO valve drive and the 24 V feed both behave differently from the specified design (e.g. an unswitched pass FET in the main rail rather than the ATO switch).

parsed.summary: The design files contain at least one real deviation: the clock buffer U8 is wired with its input on the EC isolator U4's primary SCL and its push-pull output on the shared I2C_SCL bus, so SCL is driven by both the ESP32 and U8 and U4 is left without the master clock. A second, lower-confidence discrepancy is that the AON6407 T3, which the specification describes as the ATO-valve switch driven from ATO_VALVE, is instead wired as a pass element in the main 24 V feed, with the valve actually switched by T5.
